texts.preamble: Sharada vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 25 October, 2024 Scch-21 1 Mvc No.6384/2022 Kabc0B0016472022 In The Court Of Xvii Addl. Judge, Court Of Small Causes & Member, M.A.C.T, Mayo Hall Unit, Bengaluru (Scch-21) Present: Vijaykumar S. Hiremath., L.Lb., Xvii Addl. Judge, Court of Small Causes & Member, M.A.C.T., Bengaluru. Dated this the 25th Day of October-2024 M.V.C. No.6384/2022 Petitioner/s: 1. Smt. Sharada W/o Krishnappa, Aged about 58 years, Residing at No.166, Horamavu Agara, Horamavu, Bangalore-560 043. (By Sri. T. Manjunatha, Adv.,) Vs. Respondent/s: 1. M/s New India Assurance Co. Ltd., Motor Claims Hub, No.09, 2nd Floor, Mahalakshmi Chambers, M. G. Road, Bangalore-560 001. [Policy No. 67140131220100001087 Valid Upto: 30.07.2022 to 29.07.2023] (By Smt. T. N. Malathi, Adv.,) 2. Dr. Balasubramanyam B. V S/o Venkatagiri, No.64, 10th Main, Lakkasandra Extension, Bangalore-560 030. Scch-21 2 Mvc No.6384/2022 [Owner of the Car No. Ka-05-Ml-7539] (By Smt. Sowmya. A. V, Adv.,) Date of institution of the : 21.11.2022 petition Sharada vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 25 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159131274/ 1 Nature of the Petition : U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act Date of commencement of : 17.11.2023 recording of the evidence Date on which the Judgment : 25.10.2024 was pronounced Duration of the Petition Year/s Month/s Day/s 01 09 20 Judgment
texts.facts: The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- for the accidental injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident took place on 25.10.2022. 2. The Brief facts of the petitioner's case is as under: It is the case of the petitioner that on 25.10.2022 at about 3.00 p.m., petitioner was travelling as a pillion rider in a Bullet bearing No. KA-03-JK-1831 ridden by its rider slowly and cautiously, proceeding on Bandapura Medrich company, near Avalahalli- Budigere cross road, Bidarahalli Hobli, Bangalore, at that time Car bearing Reg. No.KA-05-ML-7539 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner at a high speed and dashed to the bullet. Due to the sudden impact, the petitioner and rider fell down and sustained several grievous injuries on vital parts of the body. Immediately, the petitioner was shifted to Geetha Hospital for first aid treatment and thereafter shifted to Sundar Hospital, wherein she was treated as inpatient and petitioner has spent more than Rs.5,00,000/- towards medical expenses, conveyance, food, transport and other charges, further he require one more surgery for removal of implants. The petitioner further submitted that, prior to the accident he was heal and healthy and aged about 58 years, the petitioner was a house wife. Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner is not able to do job and hence lost her earnings. Respondent No.1 is the insurer of the offending vehicle and Respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle. Hence, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner. Hence, the petitioner has filed this petition for a compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest. 3. After service of notice, both the respondents have appeared before the Court through their counsels. But inspite of grant of sufficient opportunity, respondent No.2 not filed the written statement. The respondent No.1 filed written statement by denying the contents of the claim petition and also denying the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle. Further, this respondent submits that, at the time of alleged accident the driver was not holding Driving License to drive the vehicle. It Sharada vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 25 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159131274/ 2 is submitted that in reply, RTO Bengaluru has confirmed that the details of the said Driving License bearing DL No. KA05212240607 is not available with them. Further, the class of vehicle he is authorized to drive as per the said fake Driving License is abbreviated as 'MSWG' for the class of vehicle Motor Cycle with Gear, which otherwise is abbreviated as 'MCWG' by RTO's which itself suggests and substantiate that the Driving License is fabricated and a fake one. It is further submitted that, a police complaint has been lodged in this regard intimating the police that the Driving License produced by Shri. Bablukumar S/o Mahendra Puddari accused in Crime No.0415/2022 of Avalahalli Police Station, Hosakote Sub-Division, Bengaluru is a tampered and fake Driving License. It is furthe submitted that the 'B' Extract of the accused vehicle Car bearing Reg. No. KA-05-ML-7539 obtained by this respondent indicate the name of the accused shri. Bablukumar S/o Mahendra Poddar as the owner of the vehicle . The accused intentionally has tampered the Driving License by creating a fake driving license to escape from liability to pay compensation. Further, this respondent is not a proper and a necessary party for adjudication of the claim. The petition is bad for misjoinder of party and the accused, the owner of the Car bearing Reg. No. KA-05-ML-7539 as on the date of accident is a necessary party and is bad for non-joinder of party and the claim petition is liable to be dismissed. Further, this respondent accepts the issuance of policy inrespect of the Car bearing Reg. No. KA-05-ML-7539 and liability if any is subjected to the terms and conditions of the policy. He also denied the age, occupation and income of the petitioner. The petitioner colluding with a owner and police filed the false case. By these reasons, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.
texts.arguments: 16. In a claim of compensation U/s.166 of M.V.Act 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Honble Apex Court in Kusum and others Vs. Satveer and others reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319. 17. On the other hand the petitioner has produced the sufficient documentary and oral evidences to prove that accident was due to rash and negligent Sharada vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 25 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159131274/ 5 driving by the driver of Car bearing Reg. No. KA-05-ML-7539 and resulted in grievous injuries to petitioner. The petitioner has pleaded in the petition that he has spent huge amount towards medical expenses. In support of his plea, he has produced 13 medical bills which are marked at Ex.P.7 to the tune of Rs.2,05,425/-. Hence, looking to the injuries sustained and treatment taken by the petitioner. The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,05,425/- towards medical expenses. 21. LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID UP PERIOD: The petitioner has produced Ex.P.6 Discharge summary issued by Sundar Hospital, Bengaluru, it reveals that, the petitioner took treatment from the said hospital from 25.10.2022 to 03.11.2022 i.e. for 09 days. Hence, at least 2 months is required to recover from the accidental injuries. It is further contended that, the injured petitioner was a housewife. So, in the absence of any evidence in respect of the income of the petitioner, the petitioner might have monthly income at Rs.15,500/- as per the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka fixed notional income of the year 2022 at Rs.15,500/- per month for determination of income before Lok-Adalat for the Districts coming under the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Bengaluru Bench. The accident is of the year is 2022. Hence, the income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.15,500/- p.m. as per above decision. Hence, 2 months is to be considered as loss of income. Hence, she is entitled for compensation of Rs.31,000/- under this head. But the judgment of the Apex court in Beli Ram Vs. Rajinder Kumar and Another [AIR 2020 SC 4453] wherein the Apex Court observed as under:- "Motor Vehicles Act (59 of 198), S.149 (2)(ao(ii), S.15 - Insurer's liability - Non-renewal of driving licence - Respondent - Claimant employed as driver met with accident while driving truck owned by employer - License not renewed for period of three years and that too in respect of commercial vehicle like truck - employer cannot wash his hands off responsibility of not checking up whether the driver has renewed Sharada vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 25 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159131274/ 8 license - Gross negligence on part of employees as insured in verifying driving license, Insurance Company not liable to pay compensation." U/sec 3 of M.V Act and also meaning and definition of 'Effective driving licence' viz a viz section 3, 4 and 5 of M.V Act, whereby the insurance company has done all its efforts in establishing the fact that there was a fundamental breach of policy condition. If a person drives the vehicle without a driving license or the owner allows the person to drive the vehicle without driving license there is a breach of section 3 of M.V Act which would no doubt make the owner liable for the consequences as per the M.V act and as per the section 181 of M.V Act. 27. Therefore, judgment in MFA No. 22781/2012 C/w MFA No. 22539/2012 (MV) in a case The Divisional Manager, Reliance General Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Shri Arjun Datatray Gurav and another, wherein it is held that when there is fundamental breach of the policy condition the legibility fix on the insurance company. Therefore, this being the violation of the policy conditions while considering the liability. 28. Further this court has relied upon the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme court of India 2022 LiveLaw (SC) 932 in a case of Balu Krishna Chavan Vs. The Reliance General Insurance Company Ltd. & others wherein held that if the liability of the insurance company is decided and they are held not to the liable, ordinarily, there shall be no direction to "pay and recover", Further in para No.8 held that hence, the only aspect for out consideration herein, is as to whether in the facts and circumstances of the present case, an order to direct the Insurance Company to "pay and recover", is required to be made. On this aspect, the law is well settled that if the liability of the Insurance Company is decided and they are held not to be liable, ordinarily, there shall be no direction to "pay and recover". As far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, I have relied on a decision reported in M.F.A. No.100090 of 2014 in between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others V/s The Divisional Manager, Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has awarded interest at the rate of 6%.
